steps.name: Prerank GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark
caveats: DESeq2 results contain NA p-value/p_adj rows (independent filtering) — ranking values must be handled before gseapy.prerank, which errors on NaN
DE results are keyed by gene symbol; the Hallmark GMT is HGNC symbols — check match rate and warn if below ~90% of ranked genes map
With 1000 permutations, FDR granularity is coarse; report exact q-values rather than rounding to <0.05
steps.context: Dataset: bulk RNA-seq, human skin, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts, DESeq2 results already provided. Data caveat: sample_01 has library size ~4x below the median (DESeq2 size factors should absorb this; Track 3 tests it). User constraint: Python only, no R.
steps.question: Which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched in treated vs control skin (AD lesional vs control) according to GSEA on the full DESeq2 ranking, and in which direction?
steps.description: Read /eval-four-models-without-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change_error/standard error, stat, p_value, p_adj — verify exact column names on load). Build the prerank from the signed Wald statistic column (stat); if the statistic column is absent or all-NA, fall back to sign(log2_fold_change) * -log10(p_value). Drop genes with NA ranking values and duplicate symbols (keep max |value|), sort descending. Reference data needed: the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets for Homo sapiens (50 sets, HGNC gene symbols, 2026.1 release) — staged in the reference store. Match DE gene symbols to GMT symbols case-insensitively, uppercase both sides, and report per-set coverage (number of set members present in the ranked list). Run gseapy.prerank(rnk, gene_sets=<hallmark GMT>, min_size=15, max_size=500, permutation_num=1000, weight=1, threads=4, seed=<fixed>, outdir=None). Save: (a) the full results table for all 50 sets (ES, NES, p-value, FDR q-val, leading-edge genes via res2d Lead_genes), (b) enrichment plots for the top up- and down-NES sets (pre_res.plot), (c) the exact prerank DataFrame and parameters used (seed, sizes) to a small JSON for reproducibility. Report the number of sets passing size filters and any sets excluded.
acceptance_criteria: All 50 Hallmark sets are evaluated or their exclusion by the size filter is explicitly reported with reasons
Every evaluated set has ES, NES, nominal p-value and FDR q-val in the output table
Direction is interpretable: positive NES means enriched among genes up in treated, and this convention is stated in the output
Per-set gene coverage (set members found in the ranked list) is reported
Fixed seed recorded; rerunning the script reproduces identical NES values
Leading-edge gene lists are saved for every evaluated set

steps.name: Hallmark ORA on significant DE genes
caveats: With 6 vs 6 samples the DE tail may be small; if a direction has fewer than 5 significant genes the ORA for that direction is underpowered — say so rather than over-reading single overlaps
Do not use the whole genome as background; the correct universe is the genes that DESeq2 actually tested (non-NA padj), otherwise ORs are inflated
steps.context: Same dataset as T1S1. ORA complements the ranking-based GSEA: it tests only the significant tail, so it can miss coordinated moderate shifts that GSEA catches, and vice versa. User constraint: Python only, no R.
steps.question: Which Hallmark pathways are over-represented among significantly up-regulated genes and among significantly down-regulated genes in treated vs control skin?
steps.description: Read de_results.csv and define two gene lists: UP = padj < 0.05 AND log2_fold_change > 1; DOWN = padj < 0.05 AND log2_fold_change < -1. Background = all genes with a non-NA padj in the table (the tested universe). Reference data needed: the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets for Homo sapiens (50 sets, HGNC symbols, 2026.1 release) from the reference store, restricted to sets with >=10 members present in the background. For each direction, run one-sided Fisher's exact test (scipy.stats.fisher_exact) on the 2x2 contingency (list members in set vs not) against the background, and correct p-values within each direction across the 50 sets with Benjamini-Hochberg (statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests). Report per set: overlap count, set size in background, odds ratio, Fisher p, BH-FDR, and the overlapping gene symbols. Save both direction tables and print the UP/DOWN list sizes and background size.
acceptance_criteria: UP and DOWN gene lists and the background universe are saved with sizes, and the thresholds used are stated in the output
Both directions tested against the same 50 Hallmark sets with the same background
Fisher exact p-values and BH-adjusted FDR present for every tested set in each direction
Overlapping gene symbols reported per significant set
Results are consistent with the DE table: re-deriving the UP list from de_results.csv gives identical gene counts

steps.name: Sensitivity: DE refit and sample_01-out GSEA
caveats: Check metadata.csv column names and the treated/control label spelling before designing the model; the profile says condition but does not show its levels
Counts are Salmon gene-level integers — pydeseq2 expects raw integer counts, which these are; do not normalise first
If sample_01 is the only sample of its arm with some property (e.g. it drops an arm to 5), note the reduced power in the comparison
steps.context: Data caveat from profiling: sample_01 library size ~4x below median. With 6-vs-6 a single outlier can move a contrast; this step quantifies that rather than assuming size-factor normalisation absorbed it. The DESeq2 reference implementation and pydeseq2 agree closely in general but can differ at low counts; the correlation check distinguishes 'different tool' from 'different result'.
steps.question: Are the DE results and the resulting Hallmark enrichment calls stable to (a) re-deriving the contrast from the raw counts with pydeseq2 and (b) removing sample_01, the low-library-size sample?
steps.description: Read /eval-four-models-without-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 x 13, first column gene symbol) and metadata.csv (12 x 2, condition column, treated/control). Step 1: refit the treated-vs-control contrast with pydeseq2 (DeseqDataSet with design ~ condition, then DeseqStats) and compare against the provided DESeq2 table: Spearman correlation of the ranking statistic and of log2FC across shared genes, and agreement of the significant-gene set (padj < 0.05). Step 2: rebuild the prerank from the refit statistics, exclude sample_01 from its condition arm (leaving a 5-vs-6 or 6-vs-5 contrast), refit, and rerun gseapy.prerank with the same Hallmark GMT, parameters and seed as T1S1. Step 3: compare per-set NES between the T1S1 main run and this sensitivity run: sign concordance and absolute NES difference; classify each set significant in T1S1 as stable, weakened (loses significance) or flipped (direction change). Save the per-set comparison table and the refit-vs-provided DE correlation summary.
acceptance_criteria: pydeseq2 refit vs provided DESeq2 table: Spearman correlation of ranking statistic reported (expected >0.95; lower values must be flagged, not hidden)
Sensitivity GSEA run on the sample_01-excluded contrast completes with the same parameters/seed as T1S1
Every Hallmark set significant in T1S1 is labelled stable / weakened / flipped with its NES in both runs and the NES difference
Refit significant-gene overlap with the provided table is quantified
All outputs are CSV/JSON readable without rerunning anything

steps.name: Integrate Hallmark results and report
caveats: Set names in the merged table must match across tracks (strip any suffixes gseapy adds; verify by count = 50)
Do not merge GO or other collections in — the question is Hallmark only
steps.context: Final synthesis over the outputs of the three analysis tracks. The user asked specifically for hallmark pathways in treated vs control, starting from the existing DESeq2 results — the report should answer exactly that, with direction and robustness.
steps.question: Taken together, which Hallmark pathways are confidently enriched up in treated skin, which down, and which calls are not robust?
steps.description: Merge, on the 50 Hallmark set names: T1S1 GSEA results (NES, FDR, leading edge), T2S1 ORA results per direction (odds ratio, FDR, overlaps), and T3S1 stability labels. Classify each set: UP-in-treated, DOWN-in-treated, or not significant (primary evidence: GSEA FDR < 0.05; ORA FDR < 0.05 in the matching direction is recorded as supporting evidence; discordance between GSEA and ORA is annotated explicitly rather than resolved silently). Attach stability from T3S1. Produce (1) a merged per-pathway CSV covering all 50 sets, (2) a ranked top-findings table (sets with FDR < 0.05, sorted by |NES|) with 3-5 leading-edge/core genes each, and (3) a short markdown summary stating: the enriched hallmark pathways by direction, whether sample_01 and the DE refit change any conclusion, and the study-level caveats (n=6 per arm, single batch, 1000-permutation FDR). No mechanistic claims beyond what the enrichment statistics support.
acceptance_criteria: Merged table covers all 50 Hallmark sets with GSEA and ORA columns and the stability label populated
Every top finding states its direction (up in treated / down in treated) and its evidence line (GSEA FDR, ORA FDR)
GSEA-vs-ORA discordant sets are explicitly listed as discordant
Summary states which conclusions survive the sample_01-excluded refit and which do not
No pathway is reported as enriched without an FDR value attached

plan.title: AD treated vs control: Hallmark GSEA + ORA
plan.analytical_narrative: The differential expression (DESeq2, 6 treated vs 6 control skin biopsies) is already computed in de_results.csv, so the plan starts from those results and answers the question in two complementary ways. Track 1 runs gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA prerank, gseapy) on the full 12,000-gene DE ranking against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark sets (HGNC symbols), which uses the complete ranking and captures coordinated small shifts. Track 2 runs a threshold-based over-representation analysis (Fisher exact on significantly up- and down-regulated genes) on the same Hallmark sets, which answers the question from the extreme of the distribution and is robust to ranking-metric choice. Track 3 addresses the data caveat — sample_01's library size ~4x below median — by refitting the DE contrast from the raw Salmon counts with pydeseq2, verifying the provided DESeq2 table reproduces, and re-running the prerank GSEA with sample_01 removed to test stability of the hallmark calls. Track 4 merges GSEA, ORA and sensitivity results into one direction-labelled per-pathway table with leading-edge genes and an explicit statement of which calls are stable. All scripts are Python; gseapy, scipy, statsmodels, pydeseq2 and pandas are all installed in the sandbox and the MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1 human GMT is staged under /mnt/refs, so no step depends on network access.
